title: Hawkins on Ellington's Mood Indigo and Check and Double Check
summary: Hawkins tells Tate how he first heard Ellington on the car radio and how the film eclipsed Henderson's band.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Then I'll tell you what Hawk told me one time. He says, -- they were playing down on Broadway and Duke was playing uptown. So, you know, wherever Duke landed, he couldn't -- Fletcher would cut him all to pieces, they tell me, you know, he wasn't popular and things like that. So Fletcher got all the credit, you know. So he said, they were playing, they weren't even listening to anybody, you know, Fletcher got a little chesty, I guess, he said they wouldn't even listen to anybody. He said he'd go home at night and they were broadcasting from the Cotton Club uptown, Duke was, you know, so he says his wife says, 'You ever listen to Duke? They got

something different. You ought to listen to him." He says, "Oh, no, I'm with Fletcher Henderson, man. Nobody like Fletcher Henderson." So he said she kept bugging him and "I had a radio in my car." He said one intermission one night, after so long of her keep bugging him -- they worked anytime they wanted to, you know, down Roseland, you know, on Broadway. So he says one night he went out and he turned the radio on and they was doing something like "Mood Indigo." He says, "I hear this moody trombone and I ain't never heard nothing like that," he said, "in my life." You know, because he says, Smack knew how to voice, but he didn't"-- Duke had come up with something different, you know, like with the clarinet and the muted trumpet and the mutes.

So he says, "Man," he says, "it scared me. It scared me to death. So I went and told Smack. I says, 'Smack, if you get a chance, come sit down in the car with me and listen. Duke got something going.' Smack said, 'Man, I don't want to play uptown. I don't want to hear nothing about it.'" He didn't want to play up in Harlem. "We're on Broadway. I don't want to hear nothing about it." He says, "I think you should listen."

He said he couldn't get him to listen. So he said one night, he finally got him to listen and he was surprised, too. Said he was, you know, really excited. So he says, "Wait a minute. What is that he got?" He was trying to see

how he had this voice, but he never did come up with it, you know how Duke had had these things voiced. So Hawk told me that somehow, they lucked up and got this break in that picture with Amos and Andy, "Check and Double Check," he said, "And after that, he wiped us completely out." He said, "He ain't looked back." You know, "Check and Double Check?" He said he was on his way. He told me that himself.

Hawk told me, he says, "Buddy," he says, "after that," he says, "man, I started hearing, talking about this Jungle Band, he called his band the jungle music and things like that," he said, "but man, after they made that picture, 'Check and Double Check,'" he say, "we were on our way out."
